uncited: *   **Input:** Measured Zernike coefficients $a_{jo}$ for a set of object points; object position $\vec{o}$; hologram plane geometry.
*   **Output:** Complex phase function $f_z(\rho, \theta)_o$ for each object point, which modulates the hologram to correct aberrations.
*   Coefficients $a_{jo}$: Array of floating-point values representing the magnitude of each Zernike term for object point $o$.
*   Polar coordinates $(\rho, \theta)$: Normalized radius and angle relative to the center of the sub-hologram for object point $o$.
**Calibrate Coefficients:** Determine the measured Zernike coefficients $a_{jo}$ for a sparse set of object points via user feedback (see Subtopics).
*   **Measurement Impracticality:** It is impractical to measure $f_z$ for all millions of object points.
The display presents a single object point $o$ to the user, represented in the hologram as $f_z(\rho, \theta)_o$.
The user adjusts the coefficients $a_{jo}$ until the most tightly focused spot is seen.
This process is repeated for additional object points $o$.
Interpolation of coefficients for unmeasured points adds a lookup/interpolation step.
